sanskrit: khanakena tu tenaiva veśma śodhayatā bilam pāṃsubhiḥ pratyapihitaṃ puruṣais tair alakṣitam
english: The tunnel which that very digger had made while clearing the house was filled in with earth and left unseen by those men.

sanskrit: tatas te preṣayām āsur dhṛtarāṣṭrasya nāgarāḥ pāṇḍavān agninā dagdhān amātyaṃ ca purocanam
english: Then the townspeople sent word to Dhṛtarāṣṭra that the Pāṇḍavas and the minister Purocana had been consumed by fire.

sanskrit: śrutvā tu dhṛtarāṣṭras tad rājā sumahad apriyam vināśaṃ pāṇḍuputrāṇāṃ vilalāpa suduḥkhitaḥ
english: King Dhṛtarāṣṭra, hearing that most grievous news — the destruction of the sons of Pāṇḍu — lamented in deep sorrow.

sanskrit: adya pāṇḍur mṛto rājā bhrātā mama sudurlabhaḥ teṣu vīreṣu dagdheṣu mātrā saha viśeṣataḥ
english: "Today my brother King Pāṇḍu, so rare and dear, is truly dead — for those heroes have been burned together with their mother."

sanskrit: gacchantu puruṣāḥ śīghraṃ nagaraṃ vāraṇāvatam satkārayantu tān vīrān kuntirājasutāṃ ca tām
english: "Let men go at once to the city of Vāraṇāvata to render fitting honors to those heroes and to that daughter of the king of the Kuntis."

sanskrit: kārayantu ca kulyāni śubhrāṇi ca mahānti ca ye ca tatra mṛtās teṣāṃ suhṛdo 'rcantu tān api
english: "Let them also cause auspicious and great funeral mounds to be made, and let friends honor all those who have died there."

sanskrit: evaṃgate mayā śakyaṃ yad yat kārayituṃ hitam pāṇḍavānāṃ ca kuntyāś ca tat sarvaṃ kriyatāṃ dhanaiḥ
english: "In these circumstances, whatever beneficent rites I am able to have performed for the Pāṇḍavas and for Kuntī — let all of that be done with wealth."

sanskrit: evam uktvā tataś cakre jñātibhiḥ parivāritaḥ udakaṃ pāṇḍuputrāṇāṃ dhṛtarāṣṭro 'mbikāsutaḥ
english: Having spoken thus, Dhṛtarāṣṭra, son of Ambikā, surrounded by his kinsmen, then performed the water-offering for the sons of Pāṇḍu.

sanskrit: cukruśuḥ kauravāḥ sarve bhṛśaṃ śokaparāyaṇāḥ viduras tv alpaśaś cakre śokaṃ veda paraṃ hi saḥ
english: All the Kauravas wept aloud, wholly given over to grief; but Vidura grieved only a little, for he knew the higher truth.

sanskrit: pāṇḍavāś cāpi nirgatya nagarād vāraṇāvatāt javena prayayū rājan dakṣiṇāṃ diśam āśritāḥ
english: The Pāṇḍavas, having escaped from the city of Vāraṇāvata, O king, swiftly journeyed on, keeping to the southern direction.

sanskrit: vijñāya niśi panthānaṃ nakṣatrair dakṣiṇāmukhāḥ yatamānā vanaṃ rājan gahanaṃ pratipedire
english: Discerning their path by the stars at night, facing southward and pressing hard, they entered a dense forest, O king.

sanskrit: tataḥ śrāntāḥ pipāsārtā nidrāndhāḥ pāṇḍunandanāḥ punar ūcur mahāvīryaṃ bhīmasenam idaṃ vacaḥ
english: Then the sons of Pāṇḍu, exhausted, tormented by thirst, and blinded by sleep, spoke again these words to the mighty Bhīmasena:

sanskrit: itaḥ kaṣṭataraṃ kiṃ nu yad vayaṃ gahane vane diśaś ca na prajānīmo gantuṃ caiva na śaknumaḥ
english: "What could be more wretched than this — that we wander in a dense forest, knowing not the directions and unable to walk?"

sanskrit: taṃ ca pāpaṃ na jānīmo yadi dagdhaḥ purocanaḥ kathaṃ nu vipramucyema bhayād asmād alakṣitāḥ
english: "And we do not know whether that wicked Purocana has been burned; how can we escape this fear while remaining unseen?"

sanskrit: punar asmān upādāya tathaiva vraja bhārata tvaṃ hi no balavān eko yathā satatagas tathā
english: "Take us up again as before and carry us, O Bhārata — for you alone among us are strong, like the ever-moving wind."

sanskrit: ity ukto dharmarājena bhīmaseno mahābalaḥ ādāya kuntīṃ bhrātṝṃś ca jagāmāśu mahābalaḥ
english: Thus addressed by the king of dharma, the immensely powerful Bhīmasena took up Kuntī and his brothers and departed swiftly.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca tena vikramatā tūrṇam ūruvegasamīritam pravavāv anilo rājañ śuciśukrāgame yathā
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: As he strode swiftly, a wind arose driven by the speed of his thighs, O king, like the wind at the onset of the bright autumn season.

sanskrit: sa mṛdnan puṣpitāṃś caiva phalitāṃś ca vanaspatīn ārujan dārugulmāṃś ca pathas tasya samīpajān
english: He crushed the flowering and fruit-bearing forest trees and snapped the wooden shrubs that stood along his path.

sanskrit: tathā vṛkṣān bhañjamāno jagāmāmitavikramaḥ tasya vegena pāṇḍūnāṃ mūrccheva samajāyata
english: Thus breaking trees, he of measureless valor strode on; by his speed, something like a swoon came over the Pāṇḍus.

sanskrit: asakṛc cāpi saṃtīrya dūrapāraṃ bhujaplavaiḥ pathi pracchannam āsedur dhārtarāṣṭrabhayāt tadā
english: And again and again crossing wide rivers by the paddle of his arms, they reached a concealed path, driven by fear of Dhṛtarāṣṭra's son.

sanskrit: kṛcchreṇa mātaraṃ tv ekāṃ sukumārīṃ yaśasvinīm avahat tatra pṛṣṭhena rodhaḥsu viṣameṣu ca
english: With great difficulty he carried on his back that one delicate and illustrious mother over the steep and uneven river banks.

sanskrit: āgamaṃs te vanoddeśam alpamūlaphalodakam krūrapakṣimṛgaṃ ghoraṃ sāyāhne bharatarṣabhāḥ
english: Those bulls of the Bhāratas arrived at a region of the forest scarce in roots, fruits, and water, full of fierce birds and beasts, dreadful, toward evening.

sanskrit: ghorā samabhavat saṃdhyā dāruṇā mṛgapakṣiṇaḥ aprakāśā diśaḥ sarvā vātair āsann anārtavaiḥ
english: The twilight was terrible; the beasts and birds were fearsome; all directions were dark; and unseasonable winds blew.

sanskrit: te śrameṇa ca kauravyās tṛṣṇayā ca prapīḍitāḥ nāśaknuvaṃs tadā gantuṃ nidrayā ca pravṛddhayā
english: Those scions of the Kuru line, tormented by fatigue and thirst and overwhelmed by mounting sleep, could not walk on.

sanskrit: tato bhīmo vanaṃ ghoraṃ praviśya vijanaṃ mahat nyagrodhaṃ vipulacchāyaṃ ramaṇīyam upādravat
english: Then Bhīma, having entered that vast, desolate, dreadful forest, ran toward a great banyan tree with wide shade, lovely and inviting.

sanskrit: tatra nikṣipya tān sarvān uvāca bharatarṣabhaḥ pānīyaṃ mṛgayāmīha viśramadhvam iti prabho
english: Having set them all down there, that bull of the Bhāratas said, "I will seek water here; rest yourselves, O lord."

sanskrit: ete ruvanti madhuraṃ sārasā jalacāriṇaḥ dhruvam atra jalasthāyo mahān iti matir mama
english: "These cranes that move on water are crying sweetly — I believe there is certainly a great body of water here."

sanskrit: anujñātaḥ sa gaccheti bhrātrā jyeṣṭhena bhārata jagāma tatra yatra sma ruvanti jalacāriṇaḥ
english: Permitted by his eldest brother with the word "go," O Bhārata, he went to the place where the water-birds were crying.

sanskrit: sa tatra pītvā pānīyaṃ snātvā ca bharatarṣabha uttarīyeṇa pānīyam ājahāra tadā nṛpa
english: He drank water there and bathed, O bull of the Bhāratas, and then brought water back in his upper garment, O king.

sanskrit: gavyūtimātrād āgatya tvarito mātaraṃ prati sa suptāṃ mātaraṃ dṛṣṭvā bhrātṝṃś ca vasudhātale bhṛśaṃ duḥkhaparītātmā vilalāpa vṛkodaraḥ
english: Having returned swiftly from a distance of just a league toward his mother, wolf-bellied Bhīma saw his mother and brothers lying asleep on the bare ground and lamented, his soul overwhelmed with grief.

sanskrit: śayaneṣu parārdhyeṣu ye purā vāraṇāvate nādhijagmus tadā nidrāṃ te 'dya suptā mahītale
english: "Those who formerly at Vāraṇāvata did not reach sleep even on the most precious of beds — today they lie sleeping on the bare earth."

sanskrit: svasāraṃ vasudevasya śatrusaṃghāvamardinaḥ kuntibhojasutāṃ kuntīṃ sarvalakṣaṇapūjitām
english: "She who is the sister of Vāsudeva, crusher of enemy hosts, the daughter of Kuntibhoja, Kuntī, honored for all auspicious marks —"

sanskrit: snuṣāṃ vicitravīryasya bhāryāṃ pāṇḍor mahātmanaḥ prāsādaśayanāṃ nityaṃ puṇḍarīkāntaraprabhām
english: "— daughter-in-law of Vicitravīrya, wife of the great-souled Pāṇḍu, she who always slept in palaces, radiant as the inside of a lotus —"

sanskrit: sukumāratarāṃ strīṇāṃ mahārhaśayanocitām śayānāṃ paśyatādyeha pṛthivyām atathocitām
english: "— most tender of women, fit for the most excellent of beds — behold her lying today here on the earth, where she does not belong."

sanskrit: dharmād indrāc ca vāyoś ca suṣuve yā sutān imān seyaṃ bhūmau pariśrāntā śete hy adyātathocitā
english: "She who gave birth to these sons from Dharma, from Indra, and from Vāyu — this very one lies exhausted on the ground today, so undeserving of such a fate."

sanskrit: kiṃ nu duḥkhataraṃ śakyaṃ mayā draṣṭum ataḥ param yo 'ham adya naravyāghrān suptān paśyāmi bhūtale
english: "What greater sorrow could I behold beyond this — I who today see these tigers among men lying asleep on the bare earth?"

sanskrit: triṣu lokeṣu yad rājyaṃ dharmavidyo 'rhate nṛpaḥ so 'yaṃ bhūmau pariśrāntaḥ śete prākṛtavat katham
english: "He who deserves kingship over all three worlds, that king who knows dharma — how does he lie exhausted on the ground like an ordinary man?"

sanskrit: ayaṃ nīlāmbudaśyāmo nareṣv apratimo bhuvi śete prākṛtavad bhūmāv ato duḥkhataraṃ nu kim
english: "This one, dark as a blue raincloud, peerless among men on earth, lies on the ground like a common person — what could be more sorrowful than this?"

sanskrit: aśvināv iva devānāṃ yāv imau rūpasaṃpadā tau prākṛtavad adyemau prasuptau dharaṇītale
english: "These two, who in beauty of form are like the twin Aśvins among the gods — today these two lie sound asleep on the bare ground like ordinary folk."

sanskrit: jñātayo yasya naiva syur viṣamāḥ kulapāṃsanāḥ sa jīvet susukhaṃ loke grāme druma ivaikajaḥ
english: "He whose kinsmen are not hostile, not besmirchers of the family — he lives happily in the world, like a solitary tree in a village."

sanskrit: eko vṛkṣo hi yo grāme bhavet parṇaphalānvitaḥ caityo bhavati nirjñātir arcanīyaḥ supūjitaḥ
english: "For a single tree in a village that is full of leaves and fruit becomes a shrine; without kinsmen to trouble it, it is revered and well honored."

sanskrit: yeṣāṃ ca bahavaḥ śūrā jñātayo dharmasaṃśritāḥ te jīvanti sukhaṃ loke bhavanti ca nirāmayāḥ
english: "And those who have many kinsmen who are brave and grounded in dharma — they live happily in the world and remain free of affliction."

sanskrit: balavantaḥ samṛddhārthā mitrabāndhavanandanāḥ jīvanty anyonyam āśritya drumāḥ kānanajā iva
english: "Powerful, prosperous, rejoiced over by friends and kinsmen, they live leaning on one another, like trees that grow in the forest."

sanskrit: vayaṃ tu dhṛtarāṣṭreṇa saputreṇa durātmanā vivāsitā na dagdhāś ca kathaṃ cit tasya śāsanāt
english: "But we have been exiled by the evil-souled Dhṛtarāṣṭra together with his son, and somehow escaped being burned by his command."

sanskrit: tasmān muktā vayaṃ dāhād imaṃ vṛkṣam upāśritāḥ kāṃ diśaṃ pratipatsyāmaḥ prāptāḥ kleśam anuttamam
english: "Freed from that burning, we have taken refuge under this tree — having attained the utmost hardship, what direction shall we take?"

sanskrit: nātidūre ca nagaraṃ vanād asmād dhi lakṣaye jāgartavye svapantīme hanta jāgarmy ahaṃ svayam
english: "I can see that a town is not very far from this forest. These ones must be guarded while they sleep — I myself shall keep watch."

sanskrit: pāsyantīme jalaṃ paścāt pratibuddhā jitaklamāḥ iti bhīmo vyavasyaiva jajāgāra svayaṃ tadā
english: "These ones will drink water later when they awaken, having conquered their fatigue." Having thus resolved, Bhīma kept vigil himself at that time.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca tatra teṣu śayāneṣu hiḍimbo nāma rākṣasaḥ avidūre vanāt tasmāc chālavṛkṣam upāśritaḥ
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: While they lay sleeping there, a rākṣasa named Hiḍimba was perched in a śāla tree not far from that forest.

sanskrit: krūro mānuṣamāṃsādo mahāvīryo mahābalaḥ virūparūpaḥ piṅgākṣaḥ karālo ghoradarśanaḥ piśitepsuḥ kṣudhārtas tān apaśyata yadṛcchayā
english: Cruel, a devourer of human flesh, of great valor and enormous strength, misshapen in form, tawny-eyed, fearsome, dreadful to behold, hungry for flesh, tormented by hunger — he happened to catch sight of them.

sanskrit: ūrdhvāṅguliḥ sa kaṇḍūyan dhunvan rūkṣāñ śiroruhān jṛmbhamāṇo mahāvaktraḥ punaḥ punar avekṣya ca
english: With fingers pointing upward he was scratching himself, shaking his matted, rough hair, yawning wide-mouthed, and looking at them again and again.

sanskrit: duṣṭo mānuṣamāṃsādo mahākāyo mahābalaḥ āghrāya mānuṣaṃ gandhaṃ bhaginīm idam abravīt
english: That vile devourer of human flesh, huge of body and great of strength, sniffing the smell of humans, said this to his sister:

sanskrit: upapannaś cirasyādya bhakṣo mama manaḥpriyaḥ snehasravān prasravati jihvā paryeti me mukham
english: "After a long time, food that is dear to my heart has come my way today. Fat drips down; my tongue goes around my mouth."

sanskrit: aṣṭau daṃṣṭrāḥ sutīkṣṇāgrāś cirasyāpātaduḥsahāḥ deheṣu majjayiṣyāmi snigdheṣu piśiteṣu ca
english: "My eight fangs, very sharp-tipped, so long unbearably eager to strike — I shall sink them into those sleek and juicy bodies."

sanskrit: ākramya mānuṣaṃ kaṇṭham ācchidya dhamanīm api uṣṇaṃ navaṃ prapāsyāmi phenilaṃ rudhiraṃ bahu
english: "Seizing a human throat and severing the great artery, I shall drink the fresh, warm, frothy blood in abundance."

sanskrit: gaccha jānīhi ke tv ete śerate vanam āśritāḥ mānuṣo balavān gandho ghrāṇaṃ tarpayatīva me
english: "Go, find out who these are that lie sleeping sheltered in the forest. The powerful smell of humans all but satisfies my nostrils."

sanskrit: hatvaitān mānuṣān sarvān ānayasva mamāntikam asmadviṣayasuptebhyo naitebhyo bhayam asti te
english: "Slay all these humans and bring them to me. Those sleeping in our territory need have no fear from them; you need not fear them either."

sanskrit: eṣāṃ māṃsāni saṃskṛtya mānuṣāṇāṃ yatheṣṭataḥ bhakṣayiṣyāva sahitau kuru tūrṇaṃ vaco mama
english: "Having prepared the flesh of these humans to our liking, we two shall feast together. Quickly carry out my word."

sanskrit: bhrātur vacanam ājñāya tvaramāṇeva rākṣasī jagāma tatra yatra sma pāṇḍavā bharatarṣabha
english: Understanding her brother's command, the rākṣasī hastened to where the Pāṇḍavas were, O bull of the Bhāratas.

sanskrit: dadarśa tatra gatvā sā pāṇḍavān pṛthayā saha śayānān bhīmasenaṃ ca jāgrataṃ tv aparājitam
english: Going there, she saw the Pāṇḍavas along with Pṛthā lying asleep, and Bhīmasena, the unconquered one, keeping watch.

sanskrit: dṛṣṭvaiva bhīmasenaṃ sā śālaskandham ivodgatam rākṣasī kāmayām āsa rūpeṇāpratimaṃ bhuvi
english: The moment the rākṣasī saw Bhīmasena, risen like the trunk of a śāla tree, she fell in love with him — peerless in beauty on earth.

sanskrit: ayaṃ śyāmo mahābāhuḥ siṃhaskandho mahādyutiḥ kambugrīvaḥ puṣkarākṣo bhartā yukto bhaven mama
english: "This one, dark-complexioned, long-armed, lion-shouldered, of great splendor, conch-necked, lotus-eyed — he would be a fitting husband for me."

sanskrit: nāhaṃ bhrātṛvaco jātu kuryāṃ krūropasaṃhitam patisneho 'tibalavān na tathā bhrātṛsauhṛdam
english: "I shall never carry out my brother's word laden with cruelty, for the love of a husband is far more powerful than fraternal affection."

sanskrit: muhūrtam iva tṛptiś ca bhaved bhrātur mamaiva ca hatair etair ahatvā tu modiṣye śāśvatiḥ samāḥ
english: "My brother's satisfaction from their being slain would last but a moment, whereas if they are not slain I shall rejoice for endless years."

sanskrit: sā kāmarūpiṇī rūpaṃ kṛtvā mānuṣam uttamam upatasthe mahābāhuṃ bhīmasenaṃ śanaiḥ śanaiḥ
english: She, who could assume any form at will, took on the most beautiful human form and approached the long-armed Bhīmasena slowly, slowly.

sanskrit: vilajjamāneva latā divyābharaṇabhūṣitā smitapūrvam idaṃ vākyaṃ bhīmasenam athābravīt
english: Like a creeper vine seemingly bashful, adorned with divine ornaments, she smiled first and then spoke these words to Bhīmasena:

sanskrit: kutas tvam asi saṃprāptaḥ kaś cāsi puruṣarṣabha ka ime śerate ceha puruṣā devarūpiṇaḥ
english: "Where have you come from, and who are you, O bull among men? Who are these men sleeping here, godlike in form?"

sanskrit: keyaṃ ca bṛhatī śyāmā sukumārī tavānagha śete vanam idaṃ prāpya viśvastā svagṛhe yathā
english: "And who is this tall, dark, delicate woman of yours, O sinless one, who sleeps having entered this forest as at ease as if in her own home?"

sanskrit: nedaṃ jānāti gahanaṃ vanaṃ rākṣasasevitam vasati hy atra pāpātmā hiḍimbo nāma rākṣasaḥ
english: "She does not know that this dense forest is haunted by rākṣasas; for there dwells here an evil-souled rākṣasa named Hiḍimba."

sanskrit: tenāhaṃ preṣitā bhrātrā duṣṭabhāvena rakṣasā bibhakṣayiṣatā māṃsaṃ yuṣmākam amaropama
english: "It is by that rākṣasa, my brother of wicked disposition, who desires to eat your flesh, that I have been sent here, O one comparable to the immortals."

sanskrit: sāhaṃ tvām abhisaṃprekṣya devagarbhasamaprabham nānyaṃ bhartāram icchāmi satyam etad bravīmi te
english: "But I, having set eyes on you, radiant as the embryo of a god, desire no other husband — this I tell you truly."

sanskrit: etad vijñāya dharmajña yuktaṃ mayi samācara kāmopahatacittāṅgīṃ bhajamānāṃ bhajasva mām
english: "Knowing this, O knower of dharma, act toward me as is proper; receive me who receive you, whose heart and body are smitten with love."

sanskrit: trāsye 'haṃ tvāṃ mahābāho rākṣasāt puruṣādakāt vatsyāvo giridurgeṣu bhartā bhava mamānagha
english: "I will protect you, O long-armed one, from that man-eating rākṣasa. We two shall dwell in mountain fastnesses — be my husband, O sinless one."

sanskrit: antarikṣacarā hy asmi kāmato vicarāmi ca atulām āpnuhi prītiṃ tatra tatra mayā saha
english: "For I am one who moves through the sky and can roam wherever I desire. Obtain unequaled delight here and there together with me."

sanskrit: bhīma uvāca mātaraṃ bhrātaraṃ jyeṣṭhaṃ kaniṣṭhān aparān imān parityajeta ko nv adya prabhavann iva rākṣasi
english: Bhīma said: Who, even though powerful, would abandon today his mother, his eldest brother, these younger brothers — who could do so, O rākṣasī?

sanskrit: ko hi suptān imān bhrātṝn dattvā rākṣasabhojanam mātaraṃ ca naro gacchet kāmārta iva madvidhaḥ
english: "For what man like me, overcome by desire, would surrender these sleeping brothers and his mother as food for a rākṣasa and then go away?"

sanskrit: rākṣasy uvāca yat te priyaṃ tat kariṣye sarvān etān prabodhaya mokṣayiṣyāmi vaḥ kāmaṃ rākṣasāt puruṣādakāt
english: The rākṣasī said: I will do whatever pleases you. Awaken all of them — I will gladly deliver you all from that man-eating rākṣasa.

sanskrit: bhīma uvāca sukhasuptān vane bhrātṝn mātaraṃ caiva rākṣasi na bhayād bodhayiṣyāmi bhrātus tava durātmanaḥ
english: Bhīma said: I will not, out of fear of your evil-souled brother, awaken my brothers and my mother who are sleeping comfortably in the forest, O rākṣasī.

sanskrit: na hi me rākṣasā bhīru soḍhuṃ śaktāḥ parākramam na manuṣyā na gandharvā na yakṣāś cārulocane
english: "For rākṣasas are not capable of enduring my valor, O timid one — nor are humans, nor gandharvas, nor yakṣas, O lovely-eyed one."

sanskrit: gaccha vā tiṣṭha vā bhadre yad vāpīcchasi tat kuru taṃ vā preṣaya tanvaṅgi bhrātaraṃ puruṣādakam
english: "Go or stay, O auspicious one — do whatever you wish; or send here that man-eating brother of yours, O slender one."

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca tāṃ viditvā ciragatāṃ hiḍimbo rākṣaseśvaraḥ avatīrya drumāt tasmād ājagāmātha pāṇḍavān
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Knowing that she had been gone a long time, Hiḍimba, lord of rākṣasas, descended from that tree and came toward the Pāṇḍavas.
